edits_passing_filters.hypothesis: The lead agent wasted 20-50 steps searching the filesystem for a .db/.sqlite file (glob **/*.db, ls /tmp, ls /var, find, etc.) because it did not know the warehouse is accessed only via the schema/sample/sql tools. In A-completed_jobs_gpu-0 this caused a total failure (answer=null). Adding an explicit data-access model to the lead prompt will eliminate filesystem-searching and let the lead delegate to scout/analyst immediately, improving pass rate on warehouse tasks.

The scout prompt did not tell the scout that the warehouse is accessed only via schema/sample/sql tools, so the scout (and lead) wasted steps searching the filesystem. Also, both traces showed enum columns with inconsistent casing (status: VOID/void/Void, PAID/paid) that could cause wrong answers if not normalized. Adding explicit data-access guidance to the scout and casing-normalization guidance to analyst/verifier will reduce wasted steps and prevent wrong answers on enum-filtered queries.

The sql-basics skill was too thin (5 lines) to prevent the common failure modes seen in the traces: (1) agents searching the filesystem for a database file instead of using schema/sample/sql tools, (2) inconsistent casing in enum columns causing wrong filters, (3) inconsistent GPU model names across tables. Expanding the skill with these concrete pitfalls will make the skill actually useful when agents read it, reducing wasted steps and wrong answers on warehouse tasks.
